title: Slice exits over the $75 order cap; a swing's position follows its stake (Workstream C)
body:
Workstream C of `docs/goals/LTCM_NORTH_STAR_BUILD.md`: swings that can be exited.

## What binds an exit today (read before merging)
Measured in code and on the live ledger (read-only, 07:25Z):
- `Book.check` applies the $75 cap (`rules.max_order_usd`) and the rung's `Limits.max_order_usd` only to non-reducing orders; `ltcm/risk.py` `rule_order_notional` returns early for reducing orders.
- Every sell leaves the book as `purpose="exit"` and the adapters send `X-LTCM-Purpose: exit`; `gateway/lib/gate.mjs` `reserve({exit: true})` skips both the per-order cap (`MAX_ORDER_USD` / `MAX_ORDER_USD_KALSHI` / `MAX_ORDER_USD_ALPACA` = 75) and the day-notional cap. Only `MAX_DAY_ORDERS` and the kill switch still apply to an exit. `alpaca-paper` is never metered; `kalshi-shadow` is local.
- So **no dollar cap binds an exit today**: a $200 sell would go as one $200 order and pass. What kept exits under $75 was the House's own sizing: `capital.scaled_limits` held a rung-3 position to 4/5 of the cap ($60). On the live ledger: 253 sell orders ever (all `alpaca-paper`), largest $60.01, none over $75, zero per-order-cap refusals.
- This PR makes every exit order fit the cap on the gateway's own pricing, so a bigger position no longer leans on the exit exemption (which the gateway itself calls "the floor's own claim").

## What changed
- `league/book.py`: a sell worth more than the cap is sent as SLICES:
  - each its own venue order, with a client order id derived from (plan id, slice index);
  - every slice's fills attributed to the one intent (shares and `book.fill.intent_id` are the parent intent's id), with outcome and accounting per slice (one `book.order` row set and `book.fill` per slice; only the last fill carries `flat: true`, so the evaluator still counts ONE closed trade);
  - slices sized as equal parts of at most the cap on the gateway's pricing (Alpaca market order: max(bid, ask) x 1.10, the router's own markup; a limit: max(limit, bid, ask); Kalshi: max(bid, ask) on the leg);
  - Alpaca crypto: parts that would fall under the $10 venue minimum are merged (one order slightly over the cap, never an unfillable one);
  - the plan is durable (`book.exit_plan`, private): a refused, rejected or partly filled slice leaves the rest to the next `poll`, which sizes the next slice off what is still held and not already offered;
  - a restart resumes the plan without sending any slice twice, and sends nothing before the process has reconciled once;
  - a newer accepted sell of the same instrument supersedes an unfinished plan; cancelling a slice withdraws the plan; a plan ends after `EXIT_PLAN_TTL_SECONDS` (3600) or `max(8, 3n+2)` orders.
  - Entries keep their $75 cap. After review, a REAL book also counts an entry the way the gateway will (an Alpaca market order at the touch x 1.10, a limit at its own limit) and refuses it first with the reason, and a pool of market entries is priced the same way (see "Review fix").
- `league/capital.py` `scaled_limits(staked)`: the position is half the stake (the 4/5-of-cap ceiling is gone from the POSITION); the ORDER keeps it: `min($60, max(micro order, half))`, $66 on the gateway's pricing of an Alpaca market order. Same signature and callers.
- `league/ledger.py`: `KINDS["book.exit_plan"] = False` (private: the site validates kinds).
- `league/tests/test_ladder.py`: a one-line hunk outside my area; its assertion encoded the old $60 ceiling.

## Review fix (adversarial review, Sept 23)
Finding: `scaled_limits` gave rung 3 an ORDER cap of up to $75. The gateway prices an Alpaca market order (the adapter always sends `qty`) at the ask x 1.10 against its $75 cap (`gateway/lib/router.mjs` line 229, `caps.mjs` `alpacaNotional`), so every rung-3 real-Alpaca market entry the book approved between $68.19 and $75 would have been refused with a 403. Confirmed by reading the code; latent (no rung-3 agent on real Alpaca today).
- `scaled_limits`: the order ceiling is back to four fifths of the cap (`ORDER_SHARE_OF_CAP`), $60 = $66 on the gateway's pricing, with room for the touch to move between the book's quote and the gateway's read. Only the position follows the stake.
- `Book.check` (real books only, as only real venues are metered): an entry is also counted at `_gateway_entry_price` (Alpaca market: reference x 1.10; any limit: its limit; Kalshi market: the touch) against `rules.max_order_usd`, and refused with `order of $X counts as $Y at the gateway (...)`. This also protects any other $75 order limit (the constitution's `rungs.3.max_order_usd`, the allocator's).
- `Book._net`: a pool of market ENTRIES is priced with `_cap_price` too; two $35 Alpaca buys were one $77.45 order at the gateway and both got a 403.
- Tests: `test_a_market_entry_is_held_to_the_cap_on_the_gateways_own_pricing`, `test_a_limit_entry_counts_at_its_own_limit`, `test_a_pool_of_market_entries_is_never_one_order_over_the_cap_at_the_gateway` (paper and real crypto), `test_a_kalshi_entry_counts_at_its_own_price_not_marked_up` (shadow and real Kalshi), `ScaledLimitsTest.test_every_order_passes_the_gateway_on_its_own_pricing`. All five book tests fail on the previous head and pass now. The real-book fixtures had built positions from $72 entries the gateway would refuse; they now fit, and `assert_sound` checks every order that reached the venue, entries included.

## Rollback
An older release ignores `book.exit_plan` rows and the `slice` key on `book.order`; open plans simply stop continuing (the agent or the wind-down asks again). No money state is lost.

## Tests
- New `league/tests/test_exit_slices.py`: 58 tests (31 test methods, several run per venue) over `alpaca-paper` and `alpaca` crypto and equities, `kalshi-shadow` and `kalshi` (YES and NO legs) on the fake venue, the real practice venues (`KalshiShadowBroker`, the canary's `SimBroker`), and the House's own paths (an agent's wake exit and a death wind-down).
- `league/tests/test_capital.py`: `ScaledLimitsTest`.
- Full league suite with the per-module runner: see the comment below.
